about: Design and derived figures the engine draws once per run (kind draw), derives (kind derived, formula over other figure defaults) or holds (kind fixed), from Saint Jude Setting Bible Part VI and the Parts it cites. Dollars are 1975 dollars; *_m keys are USD millions. pools is the Part VI 9.3A allocation table (family shares sum to 100). Checked by tools/check_saintjude_pools.py.

rival_agreed_keep.note: unsourced; Base weight of the new head choosing to keep him on a man who stood against him, after an agreed contest. Historical anchor: after the agreed succession in the Gambino family in 1976 the new boss kept the rival Dellacroce as underboss; keeping the losers of an agreed contest is common, sidelining the next most common. Relative to the other answers, plus the terms of rival_weights. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_civil_war_keep.note: unsourced; Base weight of the new head choosing to keep him on a man who stood against him, after the leaders of the losing side of a civil war. After a civil war or a coup the losing leaders were usually killed (the Castellammarese War, Maranzano himself afterwards, Castellano and Bilotti in 1985); the data makes killing the commonest answer here, with exile the next. Saint Jude is more violent than the historical average (the owner's word: hectic). Relative to the other answers, plus the terms of rival_weights. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_exile_resentment.note: unsourced; Exile (sending a rival away) is likelier the more he resents the head: a bitter man is better out of the city than kept. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_exile_strength.note: unsourced; Exile is likelier the stronger the rival (the men behind him make killing him costly): sent away rather than killed. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_exile_caution.note: unsourced; Exile is likelier the cooler the head (1 - his aggression and his outfit's lean toward violence): canon has a boss who loves the offender exile him instead. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_exile_resentment_gain.note: unsourced; An exiled man resents the man who sent him this much more. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_exile_fear_gain.note: unsourced; ...and fears him this much more. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

rival_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply a head follows these weights when he deals with the losers of a war at once (the usual softmax, on the weight scale). (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_loser_exile_base.note: unsourced; A made man of the losing side who led nothing is sent away: the floor weight (rank-and-file losers are more often absorbed, sometimes demoted or sent off). (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_loser_exile_weight.note: unsourced; ...plus this x the man's weight x (1 - his fear of the winner). (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

coup_exile_base.note: unsourced; A loyalist of the dead head is sent away by the man who killed him: the floor weight. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

coup_exile_loyalty.note: unsourced; ...plus this x his loyalty to the dead head x (1 - his fear of the killer): a loyalist who is too loyal to keep and too useful to kill. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

press_outside_base.note: unsourced; Each other outfit's head presses for a quick end to a succession fight or war with at least this weight whoever he likes (a neighbour's war is bad for business and brings the police), plus his liking for a front-runner, up to 1. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_press_w_outside.note: unsourced; In a civil war the other outfits' heads weigh in toward a settlement more heavily than in a contest: settlements were usually brokered by the other families (a commission or a sit-down). (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

violence_bias_vannucci.note: unsourced; The Vannucci outfit's lean toward violence, added to its men's aggression where the engine weighs a killing of a rival or a loser: canon calls the family 'quicker to violence than to talk'. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

press_w_weary.note: unsourced; Weight of weariness (1 - exp(-weeks / the matter's typical duration)) in the pressure that ends a succession contest or a civil war. Nothing ends either by the calendar: this pressure raises the weekly chance of an agreement or a settlement. Relative weights. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_w_money.note: unsourced; Weight of money spent (bribes in a contest, the cost of a war) in the pressure to end the matter. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_w_men.note: unsourced; Weight of men lost (killings among the organisation's men since the matter began) in the pressure to end it. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_w_law.note: unsourced; Weight of law heat (open cases against the organisation's inducted men) in the pressure to end it: a family under the law's eye cannot afford a long fight. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_w_outside.note: unsourced; Weight of outside pressure in the pressure to end the matter: the share of the other outfits' heads who like one of the two front-runners and want it settled. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_w_temper.note: unsourced; Weight of the leaders' even tempers (1 - their mean aggression) in the pressure to end the matter: hot men go on. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_money_scale.note: unsourced; Money spent in a contest that counts as full money pressure (1975 dollars; about one made man's year). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_men_scale.note: unsourced; Men of the organisation killed since a contest began that count as full pressure from losses. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

press_heat_scale.note: unsourced; Open cases against the organisation's inducted men that count as full law heat (the same scale the books use). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_press_money_scale.note: unsourced; Money the two sides of a civil war have spent that counts as full money pressure: a war costs far more than a contest. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_press_men_scale.note: unsourced; Men of the organisation killed since a civil war began that count as full pressure from losses. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_agree_week.note: unsourced; The most a contest's weekly chance of ending in agreement can be (before the early factor and the clarity and pressure mix): a clear front-runner under full pressure agrees within a couple of weeks once the matter is not young. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_agree_w_share.note: unsourced; Clarity of a contest = this x the front-runner's share of the backing + (1 - this) x his lead over the next (against contest_agree_lead_scale). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_agree_lead_scale.note: unsourced; A lead over the runner-up of this much counts as a fully clear lead. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_agree_w_clear.note: unsourced; The weekly chance of agreement follows (this x clarity + contest_agree_w_press x pressure), capped at 1: a clear front-runner is enough alone. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_agree_w_press.note: unsourced; ...and pressure (weariness, money, men lost, law heat, outside pressure, even tempers) can bring agreement even with no clear front-runner, so no contest goes on for ever. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_early_weeks.note: unsourced; Time scale of a young contest: the early factor is floor + (1 - floor)(1 - exp(-weeks / this)). A fast agreement is unlikely in the first days but not impossible (replaces the old two-week minimum). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_early_floor.note: unsourced; The early factor at the first day of a contest: an agreement the same week the head fell is possible at a tenth of its later chance. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_typical_weeks.note: unsourced; The typical length of a contest: it shapes the weariness curve (1 - exp(-weeks / this)) and ends nothing. Contests of years are possible; most settle in a season. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_war_early_weeks.note: unsourced; Time scale of a young contest for the chance of civil war (replaces the four-week gate): war in the first days is unlikely, not impossible. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_war_early_floor.note: unsourced; The early factor for civil war at the start of a contest. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_war_ref_share.note: unsourced; The runner-up's share of the backing at which the chance of civil war is at full strength; a smaller side makes it proportionally less likely (replaces the 0.3 gate). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_acting_standing.note: unsourced; When no heir is shown, the acting head is the man with the highest customary weight + this x his standing. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_muscle_crew.note: unsourced; In a war's contest a candidate's muscle = this x (men under him / men of the organisation x contest_muscle_scale) + (1 - this) x his aggression. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_muscle_scale.note: unsourced; Scales the men-under-him share in the muscle term (a man with a quarter of the organisation behind him counts fully). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_trait_floor.note: unsourced; A trait bends a rate or a weight around this floor: floor + trait (ambition, loyalty, greed, risk tolerance), so a man with none still acts and one with all acts half as much again. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_age_floor.note: unsourced; A head's weekly pull to settle and show his heir is the rate x (this + (1 - this) x his age factor): a young head still sometimes settles. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_customary.note: unsourced; Weight of the data's custom (the order of the roles that succeed to a post) in the head's choice of a man for a post below his own. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_post_order_decay.note: unsourced; A man of the second role the data lists for a post counts this x as a man of the first, the third this squared: custom is a weight, not a ladder. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_drop_week.note: unsourced; The most a plot's weekly chance of being dropped can be: rises with weariness, a cooled grudge and the target's temper. Nothing ends a plot by the calendar. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_drop_typical_weeks.note: unsourced; The typical life of a plot: shapes the weariness curve and ends nothing; a patient man can plot for years. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_drop_w_weary.note: unsourced; Weight of weariness in the chance a plot is dropped. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_drop_w_cool.note: unsourced; Weight of a cooled grudge (1 - the plotter's resentment of his target) in the chance a plot is dropped. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_drop_w_fear.note: unsourced; Weight of the target's aggression (fear of being found out) in the chance a plot is dropped. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_sound_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply a plotter follows his weights when choosing whom to sound out next. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_sound_w_trust.note: unsourced; A plotter sounds out first the men he trusts: weight of trust. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_sound_w_favour.note: unsourced; ...and the men who owe him: weight of favours owed. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_sound_w_cowed.note: unsourced; ...and the men who fear him: weight of their fear. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_typical_weeks.note: unsourced; The typical length of a civil war in weeks: shapes the weariness curve and ends nothing. Real mob wars ran about one to five years (Castellammarese about 1.5, the Banana War about 5, the Colombo wars 1 to 2). (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_early_weeks.note: unsourced; Time scale of a young war: the early factor for a win, settlement or split is floor + (1 - floor)(1 - exp(-weeks / this)). A war does not end in its first weeks. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_early_floor.note: unsourced; The early factor on the first day of a war. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_win_week.note: unsourced; The most a war's weekly chance of an outright win can be (reached when one side holds war_win_share of the strength): a side wins slowly, by attrition; a side with no leader left has lost outright. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_win_share.note: unsourced; The strength share at which the chance of a win is at full weight (a reference scale, not a gate: the chance runs from half the strength up to this). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_split_ref_share.note: unsourced; The weaker side's share of the strength at which the chance of a split is at full strength; a smaller side splits proportionally less often (replaces a 25% gate). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_split_ref_men.note: unsourced; The weaker side's made men at which the chance of a split is at full strength; fewer men make it proportionally less likely (replaces a gate of four). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_money_men.note: unsourced; A side's leader's full purse counts as this many men in its strength. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_side_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply a backer follows his weights when he picks a side at the start of a war. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_target_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply a side follows its weights when it picks who strikes and whom. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_tension_bitter.note: unsourced; The share of the tension between two claimants that comes from their resentment of each other; the rest is their tempers. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_loser_standing_weight.note: unsourced; A made man who is not a unit leader weighs this x his standing as a loser of a civil war (a unit leader weighs 1). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_strength_scale.note: unsourced; The men under a rival at which he counts as fully strong when the new head weighs what to do about him. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_keep_trust.note: unsourced; ...plus the rival's trust in him. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_keep_fear.note: unsourced; ...plus the rival's fear of him. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_keep_strength.note: unsourced; ...plus the rival's strength (a strong man is better kept). (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_keep_thaw.note: unsourced; A rival who is kept on resents the head this much less. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_keep_trust_gain.note: unsourced; ...and trusts him this much more. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_sideline_resentment.note: unsourced; ...plus the rival's resentment of the head. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_sideline_ambition.note: unsourced; ...plus the rival's ambition x (1 - his fear of the head): a man who still wants the seat and does not fear him is a danger to move aside. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_sideline_resentment_gain.note: unsourced; A sidelined rival resents the head this much more. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_remove_aggression.note: unsourced; ...plus the head's aggression x the rival's resentment x (1 - his fear of the head) x (1 - strength x the next weight): a hot head with a bitter, unafraid, weak rival. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

rival_remove_strength.note: unsourced; A strong rival is harder to remove: the removal weight falls by this x his strength. (B12b follow-up: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_trust.note: unsourced; Weight of trust (trust + loyalty toward the man) in a head's or leader's choice of a man for a post. The heaviest single pull with merit: such posts go to men the chooser can rely on. Weights are relative (a weighted mean). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_kin.note: unsourced; Weight of kin (spouse, parent, child, sibling) in an appointment: blood is a strong reason in a crime family and a smaller one than trust, because a kinsman is not always a reliable man. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_favour.note: unsourced; Weight of favours owed by the chooser to the man (relationship obligation) in an appointment: debts are repaid in posts. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_money.note: unsourced; Weight of the money a man could put up for the post (his purse x the share he would offer x his ambition, against appoint_money_scale): a post can be bought but money is a light reason. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_merit.note: unsourced; Weight of merit (standing, which already blends years, role and earnings, and years inducted) in an appointment: the same as trust, so a trusted man and a proven man pull equally and the chooser's temperament decides which. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_w_cowed.note: unsourced; Weight of the man's fear of the chooser in an appointment: a man who fears him is easy to control; the lightest reason, raised by an aggressive chooser. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_temper.note: unsourced; How much temperament bends the appointment weights: weight x (1 + this x (trait - 0.5) x 2) with trust and favour bent by the chooser's loyalty, money by his greed, merit by his pragmatism, fear by his aggression. A pragmatic head names the senior man, a loyal one his friend, a greedy one the man who pays. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_merit_standing.note: unsourced; Merit = (this x standing + appoint_merit_years x years inducted) / (sum). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_merit_years.note: unsourced; Seniority's share of merit (years inducted over standing_years_cap). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_money_share.note: unsourced; The share of his purse a man offers for a post (paid to the chooser through the ledger and an org_money row when he is chosen), scaled by his ambition. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_money_scale.note: unsourced; The offer that counts as 1.0 on the money term: about a made man's yearly purse in 1975 dollars. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_fallback_days.note: unsourced; A unit that has no leader and whose head has not decided after this long past due takes the best-man rule so no unit is leaderless for ever (a stuck state: no head, or one who never answers). Two money periods. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_chosen_trust.note: unsourced; Relationship points: the man chosen trusts the chooser more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_chosen_loyalty.note: unsourced; Relationship points: the man chosen is more loyal to the chooser. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_chosen_obligation.note: unsourced; Relationship points: the man chosen owes the chooser a favour. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

appoint_passed_resentment.note: unsourced; Relationship points: each man passed over resents the chooser. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_trust.note: unsourced; Weight of the head's trust in a man when he settles on an heir: the head names a man he trusts. Relative weights. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_kin.note: unsourced; Weight of kin in the head's heir: a son, brother or nephew is the natural heir in the stories this world lives on. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_favour.note: unsourced; Weight of favours the head owes the man in his heir. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_merit.note: unsourced; Weight of merit (standing, years) in the head's heir. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_customary.note: unsourced; Weight of the customary role (succ_customary_*) in the head's heir: the usual successors are favoured but not fixed. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_w_cowed.note: unsourced; Weight of the man's fear of the head: an heir who is afraid of him is safe to name. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_temper.note: unsourced; Temperament bend on the heir weights (trust by loyalty, merit by pragmatism, fear by aggression). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_min_score.note: unsourced; A head names nobody when no candidate scores this much: the contest is then left open (a head who cannot decide, or who will not). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_pick_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply the head's pick follows the scores (the engine's usual softmax): a gap of 0.1 makes the better man about 3.5 times likelier. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_form_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance that a head with no preference forms one (x 0.25 to 1 by his age): about one head in three settles in the first year, almost all in a few years, none ever need to. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_revise_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance that a head reconsiders: about every two years, so the preference moves with the relationships. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_show_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance (x 0.25 to 1 by age) that the head makes his preference visible by telling the unit leaders: a man shows it after a few years, and some die first. Many heads never do, by design: the usual outcome is then a contested succession. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_age_from.note: unsourced; The age at which a head's pull to settle his succession starts to rise. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_age_span.note: unsourced; The span over which it rises to its full value (50 to 75, the opening heads' ages). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_show_trust.note: unsourced; When the heir is shown, every other backer's trust in him moves by this (x 0.5 to 1.5 by the backer's loyalty). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_show_respect.note: unsourced; When the heir is shown, every other backer's respect for him rises by this. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

heir_show_resentment.note: unsourced; When the heir is shown, the men who would have wanted the seat resent him (x 0.5 to 1.5 by their ambition) and are looked at again. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_customary_underboss.note: unsourced; Custom: the head's deputy is the usual successor. Weight of the role in the candidate set and in the contest (the bible does not fix an order). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_customary_consigliere.note: unsourced; Custom: the head's adviser is the next usual successor, less often than the deputy. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_customary_capo.note: unsourced; Custom: a unit leader can rise to the head's seat; less than the two above. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_ambitious_standing.note: unsourced; An inducted man outside the customary roles may stand for the head's seat if his standing is at least this... (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_ambitious_ambition.note: unsourced; An inducted man outside the customary roles may stand for the head's seat only if his ambition is at least this (and his standing at least succ_ambitious_standing): only a man who wants it and has the weight to hold it. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

succ_ambitious_stand.note: unsourced; The weight of an ambitious man outside the customary roles standing in a given week (x 0.5 to 1.5 by his ambition). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_stand_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance that a man with a customary weight w stands: this x w x (0.5 + his ambition). The acting head and a shown heir always stand. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_trust.note: unsourced; Weight of a backer's trust in a candidate when he picks whom to back in a succession contest. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_kin.note: unsourced; Weight of kin in backing. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_favour.note: unsourced; Weight of favours owed to the candidate (debts). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_money.note: unsourced; Weight of the money the candidate could put up. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_fear.note: unsourced; Weight of the backer's fear of the candidate. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_merit.note: unsourced; Weight of merit. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_heir.note: unsourced; Weight of being the late head's named heir: heavy, not final. Even a shown heir loses to a rival the leaders trust and fear more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_own.note: unsourced; Weight of a backer backing himself when he stands. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_customary.note: unsourced; Weight of the customary role in backing. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_w_muscle.note: unsourced; Weight of the candidate's muscle (the men under him and his temper), counted only in a war (the head was killed by another organisation): a wartime choice weighs muscle more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_against_resentment.note: unsourced; Weight against a candidate of the backer's resentment of him. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_against_tainted.note: unsourced; Weight against a candidate who killed the head and was not backed: the stain on him. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_crew_weight.note: unsourced; A backer counts for 1 + this x (men under him / contest_crew_scale, capped at 1): a unit leader with a large crew carries more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_crew_scale.note: unsourced; The crew size at which a backer's extra weight is full. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_stick.note: unsourced; A backer keeps last week's candidate with this much extra weight, so backing does not flip each week. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_pick_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply a backer follows his weights. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_war_week.note: unsourced; The most a contest's weekly chance of civil war can be (at full tension, a runner-up at contest_war_ref_share, a contest no longer young): a war after a succession dispute is the exception. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

contest_kill_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance, x the candidate's aggression and ambition and his gap to the leader, that a candidate who is losing has the leader killed. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_force_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance (x aggression) that a leading candidate leans on a man backing another: fear on that man's relationship, so the next week's weighing moves; an outcome reached after this is called forced. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_force_fear.note: unsourced; The fear a threat adds. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_force_resentment.note: unsourced; The resentment a threat adds. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_bribe_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance (x ambition) that a leading candidate pays a man backing another; an outcome reached after this is called bought. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_bribe_share.note: unsourced; The share of his purse he pays. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_bribe_obligation.note: unsourced; The obligation the payment creates. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_lose_resentment.note: unsourced; The resentment of the winner among those who backed another. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_win_loyalty.note: unsourced; The loyalty of his backers to the winner. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_outside_weight.note: unsourced; An outside organisation's head weighs in for the candidate he likes best (as one backer of this weight). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

contest_outside_min.note: unsourced; An outside organisation's head weighs in for a candidate only if his liking (trust and respect less resentment, 0 to 1) reaches this: a head with no feeling about the candidates stays out. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_share.note: unsourced; A man who kills the head is backed when this share of the backers (those who joined his plot, plus those who would have backed him by the contest weights) stand with him: he then takes the seat. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_backed_war.note: unsourced; Even a backed coup can meet a loyalist war: this x the loyalists' share. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_unbacked_war.note: unsourced; Unbacked killer: weight of the factions going to war, x how even the sides are. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_unbacked_loyalists_kill.note: unsourced; Unbacked killer: weight of the loyalists killing him quickly, x the loyalists' share and temper. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_unbacked_contest.note: unsourced; Unbacked killer: weight of the ordinary contest running with the stain on him. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply these weights are followed. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_accept_base.note: unsourced; A loyalist accepts the new head: the floor weight of simple acceptance. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_accept_trust.note: unsourced; A loyalist accepts the man who killed his head: the weight added per unit of his trust in the killer (accept_base is the floor): a man he already trusts is easy to accept. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_accept_fear.note: unsourced; A loyalist accepts the new head: the weight added per unit of his fear of the killer: fear is a reason to submit. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_buy_base.note: unsourced; A loyalist is bought by the new head: the weight is this x the killer's purse (against coup_buy_scale) x (0.5 + the loyalist's greed). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_buy_share.note: unsourced; The share of his purse the new head pays a bought loyalist. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_buy_scale.note: unsourced; The purse share that counts as 1.0 for buying. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_buy_obligation.note: unsourced; A bought loyalist owes the new head this. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_remove_base.note: unsourced; A loyalist is removed (killed): base x the killer's aggression x the loyalist's loyalty to the late head x (1 - his fear of the killer). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_accept_fear_gain.note: unsourced; A loyalist who accepts fears the new head more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

coup_accept_resentment.note: unsourced; A loyalist who accepts the killer still resents him: the resentment points added (he accepts, he does not forgive). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_start_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance, before x ambition x (1 - loyalty to the head) x push x (0.5 + risk tolerance), that an ambitious, backed man starts a plot against a living head. A rare, temperament-driven thing, never scheduled; most plots leak or fizzle. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_heir_rate.note: unsourced; The same against a head's shown heir by a man who was passed over. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_min_standing.note: unsourced; Only inducted men of at least this standing plot. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_min_ambition.note: unsourced; Only inducted men of at least this ambition plot against a living head or heir (and of at least plot_min_standing): a plot needs a man who wants more and counts for something. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_w_resentment.note: unsourced; Push from his resentment of the target. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_w_blocked.note: unsourced; Push from the head's having shown another man as his heir (the plotter is passed over). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_sound_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance the plotter sounds out one more backer. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_leak_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance, per man sounded, that the plot reaches the head. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_ready_share.note: unsourced; The share of the backers joined at which the plotter can strike. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_strike_week.note: unsourced; Weekly chance (x aggression) he strikes once ready. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_join_obligation.note: unsourced; A man who joins is owed by the plotter. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_join_base.note: unsourced; A man sounded out joins the plot: the floor weight even with no trust or fear. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_trust.note: unsourced; A man sounded out joins the plot: the weight added per unit of his trust in the plotter (plot_respond_join_base is the floor). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_fear.note: unsourced; A man sounded out joins the plot: the weight added per unit of his fear of the plotter. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_favour.note: unsourced; A man sounded out joins the plot: the weight added per unit of obligation he owes the plotter (debts are called in). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_ambition.note: unsourced; A man sounded out joins the plot: the weight added per unit of his own ambition x (1 - his loyalty to the target). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_tell_base.note: unsourced; A man sounded out goes to the head: the floor weight even with no loyalty (a man may tell for his own safety). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_loyalty.note: unsourced; A man sounded out goes to the head (betrays the plot): the weight added per unit of his loyalty to the target x his reliability x (1 - his fear of the plotter). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_refuse_base.note: unsourced; A man sounded out refuses and keeps quiet: the weight of simply declining, the commonest answer of a cautious man. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_respond_temp.note: unsourced; How sharply these are followed. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_joined_scale.note: unsourced; Backers joined that count as 1.0 when the head weighs a plot found. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_kill_base.note: unsourced; The head weighs having a plotter killed: the floor weight (low: killing a made man has a cost). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_kill_aggression.note: unsourced; The head weighs having a plotter killed: the weight added per unit of his own aggression. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_kill_joined.note: unsourced; The head weighs having a plotter killed: the weight added per unit of how many joined the plot (against plot_found_joined_scale): a plot with many in it is a danger to end. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_kill_low_standing.note: unsourced; The head weighs having a plotter killed: the weight added per unit of (1 - the plotter's standing): a man of little standing is cheap to kill. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_exile_base.note: unsourced; The head weighs putting a plotter out of the life: the floor weight. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_exile_caution.note: unsourced; The head weighs putting a plotter out of the life: the weight added per unit of (1 - his aggression): a cautious head prefers it to a killing. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_exile_joined.note: unsourced; The head weighs putting a plotter out of the life: the weight added per unit of how many joined. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_pardon_base.note: unsourced; The head weighs letting a plot pass: the floor weight. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_pardon_fond.note: unsourced; The head weighs letting a plot pass: the weight added per unit of his fondness for the plotter (trust and affection). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_pardon_standing.note: unsourced; The head weighs letting a plot pass: the weight added per unit of the plotter's standing: a man of standing is costly to touch. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_fear.note: unsourced; The men who joined a plot that is put down fear the head more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_pardon_fear.note: unsourced; A pardoned plotter fears the head more. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

plot_found_pardon_resentment.note: unsourced; A pardoned plotter resents the head: the resentment points added. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_win_share.note: unsourced; One side holding this share of the strength wins (or the other side has no leader). (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_kill_week.note: unsourced; The most a war's weekly chance of a killing can be (at full intensity): wars are mostly lulls, hiding and sporadic hits, not a weekly bloodbath; the Castellammarese War ran about a year and a half, the Banana War about five, with a few dozen deaths in all. (B12b follow-up 2: engine/org_coup.py, engine/org_succession.py)

war_start_intensity.note: unsourced; Intensity in the first week. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_ramp_weeks.note: unsourced; Weeks to full intensity. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_dependant_weight.note: unsourced; A man not inducted counts this much against an inducted man in a side's strength. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_money_weight.note: unsourced; A side's leader's purse adds to its strength by this. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_money_scale.note: unsourced; The purse that counts as 1.0. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_leader_target.note: unsourced; A side's leader and its unit leaders are likelier targets by this. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)

war_men_target.note: unsourced; An inducted man is likelier a target by this. (B12b: engine/org_succession.py, engine/org_coup.py)
